description: Lunar Lab designs accessible, NASA-grounded educational games that train young learners to think like real astronauts and mission control engineers.
summary:
Lunar Lifeline is a zero-login, browser-based lunar mission simulator designed for children ages 7–12 to experience real habitat engineering at Shackleton Crater.
Space education for kids often celebrates rocket launches while overlooking the tough daily survival trade-offs astronauts face after landing, such as choosing whether to spend scarce battery power heating a freezing habitat or running a science drill. Lunar Lifeline addresses the challenge by turning real lunar resource management, balancing Power, Water, and Crew Health against NASA-verified hazards like solar flare storms, -230°C crater shadows, and abrasive moon dust, into a 7-day interactive game. Players command a personalized three-astronaut crew to gather lunar research while making high-stakes daily decisions and adjusting a dual-use water slider between breathable air and roof radiation shielding.
This project is important because it moves beyond simple rocket excitement to teach real Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) problem-solving, avoiding oversimplification through post-decision NASA science facts in a free format any school or home can use.
details:
What It Does

Lunar Lifeline is an interactive, story-driven survival simulator where players act as a Flight Director for a three-astronaut crew at Shackleton Crater on the Moon's South Pole. Over 7 Sols (lunar days), players must keep their crew alive, manage limited Power and Water reserves, and collect at least 50 Science Points of lunar research to bring back to Earth.

How It Works

  • Daily Research & Survival Choices: Each Sol presents a real lunar crisis, such as -230°C crater shadows, abrasive moon dust, or greenhouse crop stress, where players choose between two actions to gather research or protect the base. Every choice carries real trade-offs across Power, Water, and Health, followed by a Mission Log popup that evaluates the decision with a real NASA spaceflight fact.
  • Dual-Use Water Tank Management: Alongside daily decisions, players split one shared water tank between the Air Maker (which makes breathable oxygen via electrolysis) and the Roof Water Shield (for blocking space radiation). Setting breathable air below 40% causes oxygen loss, while leaving roof shielding below 60% during solar storms results in radiation sickness.

Benefits & Impact

  • Zero-Barrier Classroom Access: Runs instantly in any desktop, tablet, or mobile browser with no accounts, downloads, or logins required.
  • Age-Appropriate Systems Thinking: Combines real aerospace terms with plain-language explanations so 7-to-12-year-olds can learn cause-and-effect engineering without feeling overwhelmed or having to water down the concept.

What We Hope to Achieve

We want to shift how young learners view space exploration, moving beyond rocket launches to show that living on the Moon requires careful resource management, critical thinking to evaluate decisions, and scientific problem-solving.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Core Web Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
  • Interactive Graphics: Custom inline Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) for dynamic astronaut expressions, habitat shielding diagrams, and Artemis Base Camp silhouettes.
  • NASA Open Data Integration: Verified 2026 Solar Cycle 25 flare records curated from the NASA DONKI database (with an optional live API sync toggle), alongside LRO Diviner temperature data and NASA OSDR research baselines.
  • Hosting & Version Control: GitHub and GitHub Pages (https://github.com/lisasijabat-dev/lunar-lifeline).
